sections.F: Lost photons, faster routes and leaks

demos.title: A1 · Prover exactly in the middle
demos.watch: Both verifiers are 3 m away, so they send at the same moment and both signals meet at P.

demos.title: A2 · Prover closer to one verifier
demos.watch: V1 is only 1 m away, so it sends later than V0. Open the Timing tab: both still reach P together.

demos.title: A3 · Claim outside the verifiers
demos.watch: The claim is 10 m out, past V1. A cheater standing next to V1 gets both signals first and answers early. Claims must lie between the verifiers.

demos.title: A3 · Claim off to the side
demos.watch: The claim is 2 m to the side of the road. A cheater on the road is closer to both verifiers, so it passes. Two verifiers only check the position along their line.

demos.title: A4 · Prover right at a verifier
demos.watch: The claim is V0's own spot. It works, but it only proves 'someone is next to V0'.

demos.title: A5 · 3D: four verifiers around the prover
demos.watch: Four verifiers, not on one plane, surround the claim. Rotate the 3D view in the Geometry tab.

demos.title: A7 · Prover 4 cm off, inside the precision
demos.expect: Accepted every round, with a thin margin.
demos.watch: An allowance of 0.5 ns minus 0.2 ns of processing leaves about ±4.5 cm. 4 cm still fits.

demos.title: A7 · Prover 6 cm off, beyond the precision
demos.expect: Rejected every round: the answer to V1 is late.
demos.watch: 6 cm is just past the precision limit, so the honest prover's answer misses V1's deadline.

demos.title: B1 · Prover moved 3 cm (10% of light speed for 1 ns)
demos.watch: Positions are fixed during a run, so this shows where a very fast prover would be when it answers. At everyday speeds the movement within a round is nanometres.

demos.title: B2 · Prover takes 0.8 ns to respond
demos.watch: The allowance is 0.5 ns, but the prover needs 0.8 ns. Add a 'Change the time allowance' twist of 1 ns and it passes, with a blurrier location.

demos.title: B3 · V1's clock is 1 ns ahead
demos.expect: V0 accepts, V1 rejects, so the claim is rejected.
demos.watch: V1 sends 1 ns early and also stops waiting 1 ns early. Change the offset to 0.2 ns and it passes.

demos.title: B4 · V1 uses fibre and adjusts for it
demos.watch: V1's link runs at 2/3 of light speed. V1 sends about 5 ns earlier and waits 5 ns longer, so the honest prover passes.

demos.title: B4 · Fibre adjustment exploited by a cheater
demos.expect: The cheater passes every round from 70 cm away.
demos.watch: V1 allows 5 ns for fibre, but the cheater relays through open air at full speed. The spare time lets it pass from 70 cm away instead of a few cm.

demos.title: B5 · Noisy channel (15% errors)
demos.expect: About 85% of rounds accepted, the same as the best cheaters without entanglement.
demos.watch: Press Play 100 rounds. At 15% errors an honest prover looks just like a cheater.

demos.title: B6 · 60% of photons lost
demos.expect: About 40% of rounds accepted; the rest get no answer.
demos.watch: Press Play 100 rounds. When the photon is lost the prover has nothing to answer, and the verifiers time out.

demos.title: B7 · The laser sends two photons
demos.watch: With two copies, each cheater keeps one, waits for the basis and reads it correctly.

demos.title: B8 · Why many rounds matter
demos.expect: About 85% per round; almost never 100 in a row.
demos.watch: Press Play 100 rounds. Passing all 100 would happen about once in 7.5 million tries.

demos.title: C1 · Lone cheater on V1's side
demos.watch: It must answer V0 before V0's photon could reach it, so that answer is a coin flip.

demos.title: C1 · Lone cheater on V0's side
demos.watch: It gets the photon early but not the basis, so it reads it in the Breidbart basis.

demos.title: C2 · Two cheaters guessing the basis
demos.watch: Right basis half the time, a coin flip otherwise.

demos.title: C2 · Two cheaters, best possible strategy
demos.watch: No strategy without entanglement can do better than cos²(π/8) ≈ 85%.

demos.title: C3 · Eavesdropper reads and resends the photon
demos.expect: The honest prover passes about 75% of rounds.
demos.watch: When the eavesdropper guesses the wrong basis, the photon it sends on is random. This is sabotage, not impersonation.

demos.title: C4 · Cheaters who just guess
demos.watch: Each cheater answers a random bit; both have to be right.

demos.title: D1 · Teleportation with one entangled pair
demos.watch: The photon is teleported before anyone knows the basis; the fix-up afterwards is ordinary bits.

demos.title: D3 · Teleportation chain in 2D (XOR basis)
demos.watch: Splitting the basis into XOR pieces doesn't help: a chain of teleports still wins.

demos.title: D4 · Poor entanglement (50% noise)
demos.expect: About 75% of rounds, worse than cheating without entanglement.
demos.watch: The shared pair is half noise (quality p = 0.5). Teleporting through it adds errors: (1 + p)/2 = 75% right.

demos.title: D4 · Good entanglement (10% noise)
demos.watch: Quality p = 0.9. Above p ≈ 0.71 (below about 29% noise), imperfect entanglement already beats the 85% limit.

demos.title: E1 · Cheater standing at the claimed spot
demos.watch: Position checking proves where, not who. Adding a secret key would be needed to check identity.

demos.title: E3 · Someone in the middle flips the basis
demos.expect: The honest prover passes about 50% of rounds.
demos.watch: The prover reads with the wrong setting and gets random answers. The verifiers notice errors.

demos.title: E3 · Someone in the middle holds messages for 2 ns
demos.watch: Delaying only blocks the check. It can never make a cheater pass.

demos.title: E4 · Cheater right next to V0
demos.watch: Being near a verifier gives no extra advantage. It is the lone cheater of C1.

demos.title: E5 · Honest prover and cheater at the same spot
demos.expect: Accepted: the cheater got the photon and answered.
demos.watch: Both get the basis, but only one can have the photon. The honest prover is left waiting.

demos.title: F1 · Cheaters say 'no photon' when they guess wrong
demos.watch: Press Play 100 rounds and check the outcomes: lost rounds, but never a wrong bit. With real loss above 50%, verifiers can't tell this from an honest prover.

demos.title: F3 · Cheater with a straight route past a 12 m fibre detour
demos.expect: The cheater passes every round from next to V0.
demos.watch: V1 allows 50 ns for its fibre detour. The cheater takes the straight path and has time to spare.

demos.title: F4 · The basis leaks to a cheater
demos.watch: Knowing the basis early, it reads the photon the moment it arrives. Verifier secrets must stay secret.
